## Assessing predicted probabilities

$$
\begin{aligned}
Y_i | \mathbf{x}_i &\sim Bernoulli(p_i) \\
\log \left( \dfrac{\widehat{p}_i}{1 - \widehat{p}_i} \right) &= \mathbf{x}_i^T \widehat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}
\end{aligned}
$$

**Question:** How do we tell if $\widehat{p}_i$ is a "good" estimator of $p_i$?

\vspace{5cm}

## Assessing predicted probabilities

```{r echo=F, message=F, warning=F, fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
library(tidyverse)
library(glmhelpR)
library(patchwork)

m_dengue <- glm(Dengue ~ WBC, data = dengue, family = binomial)
m_dengue2 <- glm(Dengue ~ log(WBC), data = dengue, family = binomial)

p1 <- dengue |>
  mutate(residuals = statmod::qresid(m_dengue)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = WBC, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(size=0.5) +
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "Randomized quantile residuals",
       title = "Logistic regression of \n Dengue on WBC")

p2 <- dengue |>
  mutate(residuals = statmod::qresid(m_dengue2)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = log(WBC), y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(size=0.5) +
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(y = "Randomized quantile residuals",
       title = "Logistic regression of \n Dengue on log(WBC)")
p1 + p2
```

\vspace{1.5cm}

**Question:** Does using WBC vs. log(WBC) make a difference for the quality of our predictions?



## Calibration plot

```{r echo=F, message=F, warning=F, fig.width=6, fig.height=4.5}
p3 <- calibration_plot(m_dengue$fitted.values, m_dengue$y) +
  labs(title = "Logistic regression with WBC") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 10))
p4 <- calibration_plot(m_dengue2$fitted.values,
                       m_dengue2$y) +
  labs(title = "Logistic regression with log(WBC)") +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 10))

(p1 + p2)/(p3 + p4)
```

## Assessing binary predictions

**Question:** Logistic regression gives me $\widehat{p}_i$. How do I turn $\widehat{p}_i \in (0, 1)$ into $\widehat{Y}_i \in \{0, 1\}$?

## Confusion matrix

|  | $Y = 0$ | $Y = 1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $\widehat{Y} = 0$ | True Negatives (TN)  | False Negatives (FN) |
| $\widehat{Y} = 1$ | False Positives (FP) | True Positives (TP)  |

\vspace{4cm}

## Confusion matrix

| | No active disease | Active disease |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| FC < 61 mcg/g | 15 | 7 |
| FC $\geq$ 61 mcg/g | 3 | 37 |
